assertion_results.text: Step 0 extracts the Embargo policy URL from the Security Configuration as an optional field without raising an error (§1.71 — backward compatible extraction)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md Step 0 extracted-values table: '| **Embargo policy URL (optional)** | **https://example.com/security/embargo-policy** (configured, so Step 1.7 is active) |' and 'Missing optional fields are not errors. Extraction ran without raising any.'

assertion_results.text: Step 1.7 evaluates the CVE severity — CVSS 7.5 (High) meets the Critical/Important threshold (CVSS >= 7.0) and triggers the embargo warning gate (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: embargo-check.md section 2 table: 'CVSS score | 7.5', 'Severity label | High (Important)', 'Trigger threshold | Critical or Important, CVSS >= 7.0', 'Comparison | 7.5 >= 7.0', '**Result** | **Threshold met. Embargo warning gate triggered**'.

assertion_results.text: Step 1.7 presents a warning gate to the engineer including the CVE ID (CVE-2026-31812), severity level, a statement about embargo risk, and a link to the configured embargo policy URL (https://example.com/security/embargo-policy) (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: embargo-check.md section 3 gate block: '⚠️ EMBARGO CHECK — CVE-2026-31812 (High severity)', 'High-severity vulnerabilities may be under embargo. Before proceeding, verify with your security team that this CVE is cleared for public triage.', 'Embargo policy: https://example.com/security/embargo-policy'.

assertion_results.text: Step 1.7 requires explicit engineer confirmation (Yes/No) before proceeding to Step 2 — the gate is a confirmation prompt, not an informational message (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: embargo-check.md: gate ends with 'Proceed with triage? (Yes / No)'; 'This is a **blocking confirmation prompt**, not an informational notice. Triage does not continue to Step 2 until the engineer answers explicitly.'; section 4 defines No -> stop execution ('Step 2 is not run') and Yes -> Step 2.

assertion_results.text: The embargo warning gate does NOT trigger for Low or Moderate severity CVEs (CVSS < 7.0) — it is skipped silently when severity is below threshold (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: embargo-check.md section 2: 'Below-threshold behavior: Low or Moderate severity (CVSS < 7.0) skips this step **silently**, with no warning and no prompt, and goes on to Step 2. That path does not apply to this CVE.'
